insights.headline: Your certainty is highest exactly where you skip outside input, creating a 33-percentage-point accuracy collapse.
insights.evidence: On the 11 decisions rated 85%+ that you reasoned through alone, you were right only 55% of the time, compared to 88% accuracy on the 8 high-confidence decisions you talked through. In your solo entries, statements like 'I've thought about this a lot' and 'I don't need to run this by anyone' consistently act as substitutes for external input rather than evidence of rigorous checking.
insights.tryInstead: Require yourself to talk through any decision rated 85% or higher with an outside person before finalizing it.

insights.headline: Career choices are your most miscalibrated domain, where high confidence regularly masks blind spots.
insights.evidence: Across 7 career decisions, your average confidence was 84%, yet you were right only 43% of the time. Your reasoning entries show unverified self-assumptions, using phrases like 'I know my own bandwidth' or 'I'm confident I know what I'm worth' right before outcomes that resulted in burnout or under-negotiated compensation.
insights.tryInstead: Before making a career decision, commit to checking objective market or workload data rather than relying on internal intuition.

insights.headline: Your peak confidence bucket (85-100%) is significantly less reliable than your moderate confidence bucket (70-84%).
insights.evidence: You expected 89% accuracy on the 19 decisions rated 85-100% confidence, but you were right only 68% of the time, whereas you were right 100% of the time on the 5 decisions rated 70-84%. In the top bucket, your entries show you actively brushing off additional checks with language like 'I don't see the point of overcomplicating it' and 'don't need to check the math'.
insights.tryInstead: Treat feeling 85%+ certain as a red flag to search for at least one piece of disconfirming evidence before deciding.
